_note: Tiles for tools.html, rendered by scripts/build_site.py. Adding a tool is an edit here, not HTML surgery. Every tile MUST carry an `evidence` link and at least one `sector`; the build raises otherwise. Headlines are in the second person or the imperative and say what the visitor gets -- never a methods sentence. No 'hire me' register, no CV cross-links, no 'my research' framing.

sections.title: Find out something about yourself
sections.blurb: Short tasks that end with a number about you, placed against people who did the same task.

sections.title: Run your own data through it
sections.blurb: Bring a spreadsheet. These fit a model to it in your browser and hand the estimates back.

sections.title: Play the experiment we actually ran
sections.blurb: The task itself, as participants saw it.

sections.title: Just use it
sections.blurb: No paper behind these. Small tools built for a job, kept here in case the job is yours too.

tools.headline: When two of your products get confused, is it people's eyes or their standards?
tools.what_you_get: Upload identification counts; get separate estimates of how distinguishable your items are and how your respondents were deciding, each with an uncertainty range.

evidence.label: See the method and its recovery checks

tools.alt: GRIN Space Builder: plot of the perceptual space created by four stimuli

tools.headline: Has this AI ever seen anything like your photo before?
tools.what_you_get: Pick or take a close-up photo and see the model's call beside two familiarity scores — how typical your image is of what it was trained on. Images stay on your computer.
tools.caution: A research demonstration, not medical advice. We are not that kind of Doctor.
tools.alt: KITH final step: training images mapped, with two new images placed and scored

tools.headline: Eight methods papers, rebuilt as things you build instead of read.
tools.what_you_get: Commit to a prediction before each step shows you the answer, then pull the sliders yourself: likelihood surfaces, overfitting, Bayes factors, bandits, response times, simulation-based inference.

evidence.label: Every workshop cites the paper it rebuilds

tools.load_note: Runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you do is recorded, and nothing is saved between visits.

tools.headline: Read one paragraph at a time, with your notes beside it.
tools.what_you_get: Open a TXT, Markdown, TeX, DOCX or text-based PDF file and read it by paragraph, sentence or page-group, with notes anchored to the passage you were on. Play a selected passage one word at a time when the sentence will not sit still.
tools.load_note: Runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you open is uploaded, and your notes stay on this device.
tools.alt: Reader's opening screen: a paste box and file controls beside the line “Read at your own pace.”
